title: Reference-corpus bisector for cost-autotune rollback
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'bisector' evaluation harness and orchestration policy that isolates the minimal subset of prompt/categories that exhibit quality regressions after applying batching/caching or quantization-based cost recommendations. This tool will power safe progressive applies and automated rollbacks by identifying both the signals to trust and the human-audit window for edge cases.

Why: Our current acceptance harness runs broad stratified evals and golden-anchor checks but lacks an efficient way to (1) triage large candidate config diffs to the smallest failing slices and (2) produce concise artifacts for rapid human review. The bisector will reduce reviewer burden, shorten mean time to rollback, and improve confidence for higher-frequency autotune ops.

Scope:
- Implement a bisector runner that given: baseline-config, candidate-config, and stratified prompt corpus, performs hierarchical delta testing across taxonomy (intent, length bucket, template family).
- Produce a ranked "delta slice" list with metrics per slice: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), token-level edit distance, generation-quality metric (BERTScore / ROUGE/ BLEU where applicable), and a behavioral fingerprint score (model-behavior embedding drift).
- Integrate with existing canary pipeline so the orchestrator can: progressive-apply -> shadow-eval -> bisect -> notify -> gated-apply or rollback.
- Add human-audit payloads: concise representative examples per failing slice, upstream PR link, and suggested rollback justification text.
- Provide acceptance thresholds and statistical test defaults for automated decisioning (see Test Plan).
acceptance_criteria: Bisector can run end-to-end on a 5k stratified corpus within 30 minutes on standard CI workers and produce a ranked slice list.
For known regressions (internal seed set), bisector isolates a slice containing failing prompts with >90% recall relative to exhaustive delta analysis.
Orchestrator can trigger an automated rollback when top-ranked slices exceed configured thresholds without requiring immediate human intervention (configurable).
Human-audit payloads contain at most 10 exemplar prompts per slice with metadata (prompt id, user intent, baseline vs candidate outputs, embedding similarity).
Results and artifacts are persisted to the rollout dashboard and surfaced in the rollout timeline with links to PRs and historical diffs.
milestones: M1 - Bisector prototype (hierarchical slice runner, metric collectors) - 2026-03-10
M2 - Integrate with canary shadow-eval pipeline and dashboard storage - 2026-03-18
M3 - Human-audit payloads and automated decision knobs - 2026-03-22
M4 - QA run on cost-autotune experiments + rollout playbook update - 2026-03-25
implementation_notes: Use existing eval harness (ENG-31209) metric collectors but add an embedding-based behavioral fingerprint (use model-agnostic sentence embeddings).
Hierarchy: global -> intent -> template-family -> length-bucket. Bisector should support early-stopping if top slices already explain >80% of observed regression delta.
Parallelize slice evaluations with token-budget-aware batching to avoid inflating cost during CI runs.
Persist minimal artifacts (representative JSONL per slice) to object storage and surface pointers in the Linear ticket and rollout UI.
Add config knobs for: min-slice-size, min-effect-size, p-value threshold, semantic-similarity floor for grouping, and max-exemplars-per-slice.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric collectors (embedding sim, BERTScore wrapper, edit distance).
E2E smoke: run bisector on small curated corpus (200 prompts) containing seeded regressions and assert isolation behavior.
Performance: end-to-end run on 5k corpus completes in <30 minutes and memory usage stays under 12GB on CI worker.
Statistical checks: bootstrap sampling to compute confidence intervals; default rollback predicate requires effect-size > 2% loss in BERTScore or embedding-similarity drop > 0.04 with p < 0.05.
Human-Audit UX test: reviewers can label a slice as "accept"/"reject" and submit feedback which becomes training signal for future autotune decisions.
monitoring_and_rollforward: Expose bisector-derived signals as rollout metrics: top_slice_effect_size, pct_prompts_affected, semantic_drift_mean.

When any metric breaches configured auto-rollback thresholds, the orchestrator enters 'awaiting-approval' and notifies on-call + the owning team. If thresholds exceed hard-rollback limits and HIA window expires, automated rollback occurs.
Maintain historical bisector snapshots per rollout so post-mortems can compare slice evolution across config versions.
Add alerting for bisector failures or incomplete runs (CI timeout, storage errors) to SRE channel.
